7: ## 1. Purpose
8: 
9: A sports club needs a website to present the sports it offers in a clear
10: structure, to be visible online and to recruit new members. A good club website
11: also offers a simple way to sign up for a trial training session.
12: 
13: ## 2. Target Groups
14: 
15: | Target group | Need |
16: |--------------|------|
17: | Members | Find out quickly when and where training sessions and events take place. |
18: | Parents | Find out when and where events take place, and see where they can help out. |
19: | Guests / prospective members | Sign up for a trial training session quickly, and find out where league games take place. |
20: | Sponsors | Find out quickly which teams play in a high league and are worth sponsoring. |
21: | Club board (client) | Keep content such as events and news up to date without programming knowledge, and present the club and its sponsors in a positive light. |
22:

24: ## 3. Functional Requirements
25: 
26: ### F1: Start page
27: 
28: - **Description:** The start page is the first thing visitors see when they open
29:   the website, so it must be easy to understand at a glance. It presents the club
30:   with a banner, which usually contains pictures or videos of the club. Visitors
31:   must immediately see how they can join the club. Below the banner, the start
32:   page shows the latest club news, the upcoming events and a way to reach every
33:   sport the club offers.
34: - **Rationale:** If the start page is hard to understand, visitors leave the
35:   website quickly. Prospective members in particular need a direct way to join.
36: - **Priority:** Must
37: - **Acceptance criteria:**
38:   - [ ] The membership application form can be reached from the start page with
39:         one click.
40:   - [ ] The start page contains no more than five main sections.
41:   - [ ] Every sport the club offers can be reached from the start page.
42:   - [ ] Events are shown in chronological order, the earliest first.
43:   - [ ] Each event shows its name and its date in German format (DD.MM.YYYY).
44:   - [ ] Past events are not shown as upcoming.
45:   - [ ] If there are no upcoming events, a clear message is shown instead of an
46:         empty area.
47: 
48: ### F2: Top bar
49: 
50: - **Description:** The top bar is visible to visitors on every page, so it should
51:   have an unobtrusive design. From the top bar, visitors can reach every subpage of
52:   the website, most importantly every sport the club offers. Even though every
53:   subpage is reachable, the menus must stay clearly structured. Only add the menus
54:   that are actually needed: if the club offers four sports or fewer, show them
55:   directly in the top bar instead of grouping them in a menu. The Top Bar should
56:   also have the icon of the club, which navigates the visitor back to the start page.
57: - **Rationale:** Visitors use the top bar to get quickly to the page that interests
58:   them. Without it, or with a cluttered one, they cannot find their way around.
59: - **Priority:** Must
60: - **Acceptance criteria:**
61:   - [ ] The top bar is shown on every page of the website.
62:   - [ ] Every subpage can be reached from the top bar with at most two clicks.
63:   - [ ] If the club offers four sports or fewer, each sport is shown directly in
64:         the top bar.
65:   - [ ] If the club offers more than four sports, they are grouped in one menu.
66:   - [ ] There are no empty menus and no links to pages that do not exist.
67:   - [ ] The page the visitor is currently on is highlighted in the top bar.
68:   - [ ] The club name or logo in the top bar leads back to the start page.
69:   - [ ] The top bar is fully usable on a screen width of 320 px.
70:   - [ ] All entries can be reached and opened with the keyboard, with a visible focus.
71:   - [ ] Club icon navigates the visitor back the start page
72: 
73: ### F3: Sponsors
74: 
75: - **Description:** If a club has sponsors, they are presented on the website.
76:   They appear at the bottom of the page, so they do not distract visitors from
77:   the main content. If a sponsor has a website, visitors can click on the sponsor
78:   to get there.
79: - **Rationale:** Sponsors expect to be acknowledged on the club's website in
80:   return for their support. Visible acknowledgement helps the club keep its
81:   sponsors and win new ones.
82: - **Priority:** Should
83: - **Acceptance criteria:**
84:   - [ ] Every sponsor provided by the client is shown.
85:   - [ ] Sponsors are shown at the bottom of the page, after the main content.
86:   - [ ] If the club has no sponsors, no sponsor section is shown.
87:   - [ ] Each sponsor is shown with its logo if the client provided one and
88:         confirmed that it may be used. Otherwise, the sponsor's name is shown.
89:   - [ ] Clicking a sponsor that has a website opens that website.
90:   - [ ] Sponsors without a website are shown, but are not clickable.
91:   - [ ] Links to sponsor websites are recognisable as links to external websites.
92:   - [ ] Every sponsor logo has a text alternative containing the sponsor's name.
93:   - [ ] Sponsors are shown at the bottom of every page, after the main content.
94: 
95: ### F4: Sport page
96: 
97: - **Description:** The sport page is the heart of every sport the club offers.
98:   It presents the department with its own texts, pictures and videos, while still
99:   matching the overall look and feel of the website. Besides this content, every
100:   sport page shows at least all teams of the department, an overview of all
101:   training times and, most importantly, a way to request a trial training session.
102: - **Rationale:** Prospective members in particular need an easy way to request a
103:   trial training session, because this increases the chance that they join the
104:   club. Members and parents need to find teams and training times quickly.
105: - **Priority:** Must
106: - **Acceptance criteria:**
107:   - [ ] Every sport the club offers has its own sport page.
108:   - [ ] Every sport page uses the same top bar, footer, colours and fonts as the
109:         rest of the website.
110:   - [ ] Every sport page has an area for the department's own texts, pictures
111:         and videos.
112:   - [ ] Every sport page lists all teams of the department.
113:   - [ ] Every sport page shows the training times of all teams, with day, time
114:         and location.
115:   - [ ] If a department has no teams or no training times yet, a clear message is
116:         shown instead of an empty area.
117:   - [ ] From every sport page, visitors can request a trial training session.
118:   - [ ] Visitors receive a confirmation after sending a trial training request.
119:   - [ ] If a required field in the request is missing or invalid, the visitor
120:         sees a clear message explaining what to correct.
121: 
122: ### F5: Department content editing
123: 
124: - **Description:** Each department can update the content of its own sport page
125:   (texts, pictures and videos) without programming knowledge. The overall design
126:   of the page stays the same, so the website keeps a consistent look and feel.
127: - **Rationale:** Departments want to keep their page up to date themselves
128:   without asking the club board for every change. This keeps the information
129:   current and takes work off the board.
130: - **Priority:** Could
131: - **Acceptance criteria:**
132:   - [ ] Department members can change texts, pictures and videos on their own
133:         sport page without programming knowledge.
134:   - [ ] Department members can only change the sport page of their own department.
135:   - [ ] Only signed-in department members can make changes.
136:   - [ ] Department members cannot change the top bar, footer, colours or fonts.
137:   - [ ] Before a picture or video is published, the department member confirms
138:         that it may be used and that the people shown have given their consent.
139:   - [ ] Changes are visible on the website after saving.
140: 
141: ## 4. Non-Functional Requirements
142: 
143: ### N1: Legal compliance
144: 
145: - **Description:** The website has a legal notice (Impressum) and a privacy policy
146:   (Datenschutzerklärung) that visitors can always reach. The legal notice contains
147:   the information required by German law, and the privacy policy describes how the
148:   website processes personal data as required by the GDPR.
149: - **Rationale:** A club website in Germany must have both pages to be published
150:   legally. Missing or incorrect pages can lead to formal warnings (Abmahnungen)
151:   and fines.
152: - **Acceptance criteria:**
153:   - [ ] A legal notice page and a privacy policy page exist.
154:   - [ ] Both pages can be reached with one click from every page of the website.
155:   - [ ] The legal notice shows the club's name, address, authorised representatives
156:         (board), contact details and register entry.
157:   - [ ] Missing club details are shown as clearly marked placeholders, not as
158:         invented data.
159:   - [ ] The privacy policy only describes data processing that the website
160:         actually performs.
161:   - [ ] Every feature that processes personal data (e.g. the trial training
162:         request) is described in the privacy policy.
163:   - [ ] The privacy policy is marked as a draft that must be reviewed by the club.
164:   - [ ] No content from third parties (e.g. videos, maps, fonts, trackers) is
165:         loaded before the visitor has given consent.
166: 
167: ### N3: Accessibility
168: 
169: - **Description:** The website can be used by all visitors, including people with
170:   visual, hearing, motor or cognitive impairments, older members and people using
171:   assistive technologies such as screen readers. It meets WCAG 2.2, conformance
172:   level AA.
173: - **Rationale:** A sports club is open to everyone. Many clubs offer inclusive or
174:   senior sports, and their members must be able to use the website as well.
175:   An inaccessible website excludes potential members.
176: - **Acceptance criteria:**
177:   - [ ] The website meets the success criteria of WCAG 2.2, level AA.
178:   - [ ] All content and functions can be used with the keyboard alone.
179:   - [ ] All content remains readable and usable when the text is enlarged to 200 %.
180:   - [ ] Information is never conveyed by colour alone.
181:   - [ ] Videos with spoken content have captions.
182:   - [ ] Nothing plays, moves or blinks automatically for more than five seconds
183:         without a way to pause or stop it.
184:   - [ ] Texts are written in plain, easy-to-understand language.
185: 
186: ### N4: Usability and responsive design
187: 
188: - **Description:** The website is designed mobile first, because many visitors use
189:   it on their phones. On larger screens, such as laptops, it makes good use of the
190:   available width instead of showing a narrow mobile layout. Visitors find what
191:   they are looking for quickly and without explanation.
192: - **Rationale:** Members and parents often check training times or events on the
193:   go, for example on the way to the sports ground. On a laptop, a stretched
194:   mobile layout looks unprofessional and wastes space. If the website is hard to
195:   use, visitors leave and prospective members do not sign up.
196: - **Acceptance criteria:**
197:   - [ ] The website is fully usable on screen widths from 320 px to 1920 px.
198:   - [ ] No page requires horizontal scrolling.
199:   - [ ] On wide screens, content is arranged side by side where it makes sense
200:         (e.g. events and news next to each other) instead of in one long column.
201:   - [ ] Lines of running text stay short enough to read comfortably, even on wide
202:         screens.
203:   - [ ] Buttons and links are large enough to tap with a finger (at least
204:         44 × 44 px).
205:   - [ ] Links and buttons are clearly recognisable as clickable.
206:   - [ ] No information or function is available only on mouse hover.
207:   - [ ] Recurring elements (top bar, footer, sponsors) appear in the same place on
208:         every page.
209: 
210: ### N5: Performance
211: 
212: - **Description:** The website shows simple information such as events, teams and
213:   training times. Its pages should therefore load quickly, even on a mobile
214:   connection.
215: - **Rationale:** Visitors are annoyed by slow pages and often leave before the
216:   content appears. Many visitors use the website on their phones with a mobile
217:   connection, where slow pages are especially noticeable.
218: - **Acceptance criteria:**
219:   - [ ] The main content of every page is visible within 2.5 seconds on a mobile
220:         connection (Largest Contentful Paint ≤ 2.5 s).
221:   - [ ] The page reacts to clicks and input within 200 ms
222:         (Interaction to Next Paint ≤ 200 ms).
223:   - [ ] Content does not jump around while the page is loading
224:         (Cumulative Layout Shift ≤ 0.1).
225:   - [ ] Every page reaches a Lighthouse performance score of at least 90 in the
226:         mobile test.
227:   - [ ] The start page transfers less than 1 MB of data on first load.
228:   - [ ] Pictures are delivered in a size that fits the screen they are shown on.
229:   - [ ] Videos are only loaded when the visitor starts them.
230: 
231: ### N6: UI design
232: 
233: - **Description:** The website uses a bright and warm colour palette and prefers
234:   rounded shapes over sharp edges, so it looks welcoming and friendly. If the
235:   client asks for other colours (e.g. the club colours) or a different shape
236:   language, the client's wishes take precedence over this default.
237: - **Rationale:** A sports club wants to attract new members and appear open to
238:   everyone. A friendly, inviting appearance makes visitors more likely to stay and
239:   get in touch.
240: - **Acceptance criteria:**
241:   - [ ] Unless the client specifies otherwise, the website uses a bright, warm
242:         colour palette.
243:   - [ ] Unless the client specifies otherwise, buttons, cards and pictures have
244:         rounded corners.
245:   - [ ] If the client specifies colours or shapes, these are used instead.
246:   - [ ] The same colours and shapes are used consistently on every page.
247:   - [ ] All colour combinations still meet the contrast requirements of N3.
248: 
249: ## 5. Out of Scope
250: 
251: - Login and user accounts
252: - Role and permission management
253: - Connection to a real database
